AMD-SUP-2026-02 is an amendment to [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] effective 1 September 2026 that tightens the acceptance criteria for [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]][^r1][^r2]. Under this amendment, certificates must have been issued within the last 12 months and remain valid for at least 60 days following order placement[^r2]. It governs all new purchase orders placed for lithium-cell parts as of today, 26 October 2026[^r2][^r3].

| Field | Value |
|---|---|

| Version | 1.0 |

| Effective Date | 2026-09-01 |
| Status | CURRENT |

## Clauses

### 1. What changes
Effective 1 September 2026, [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] §4.4 is replaced such that a [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2]. A certificate meeting the old rule of being issued within 24 months and not expired counts as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, whereas orders released before that date are not affected[^r3].

### 2. Why
The policy change was prompted by a July 2026 incident where a battery pack lot from a supplier with a 22-month-old test report failed Northbridge's incoming abuse test because the cell maker had changed[^r4].

### 3. What purchase staff must do
Purchase staff must check the issue date and valid-to date of a lithium-cell part's certificate against the new rule before raising an order[^r5]. The [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] must run the certificate-expiry report per MAN-PUR-72 §22.6 on the first working day of each month with a 90-day window and notify every supplier whose UN 38.3 certificate expires within it[^r6]. All other parts of POL-SUP-003 §4 remain in effect[^r7].

## Versions and conflicts
- **Today's rule (effective 2026-09-01)**: For new orders placed from 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and valid for at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2][^r3].
- **Older rule (superseded)**: Certificates issued within 24 months and not expired were accepted under POL-SUP-003 §4.4; these now count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date are not affected[^r3].
- **Kind**: `superseded`[^r2][^r3].

Tax codes in Ledgerline classify VAT treatment across orders and purchase invoices based on supplier jurisdiction [^r1]. Domestic transactions use dedicated standard tax identifiers, whereas imports and cross-border purchases require specific reverse-charge treatment [^r1]. Correct application ensures accurate accounting according to [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001 Purchase Policy]] [^r1].

## What it holds
The tax code reference defines the VAT classification rules applied to purchase orders and invoices in Ledgerline [^r1]. It distinguishes between UK domestic VAT rates and reverse-charge regimes for foreign suppliers [^r1].

## Columns
* **Tax Code Suffix**: Identifies the regional tax classification applied in Ledgerline (`-UK` or `-RC`) [^r1].
* **Supplier Type**: Indicates whether the supplier is based in the UK or overseas [^r1].
* **Application**: Specifies the designated use across purchase orders and invoices [^r1].

## How to look up a row
Determine the location of the vendor; orders and invoices for UK suppliers use VAT codes ending in `-UK`, while overseas suppliers use reverse-charge VAT codes ending in `-RC` [^r1].

## Size
Two primary VAT code category suffixes (`-UK` and `-RC`) applied across Ledgerline orders and invoices [^r1].

POL-APR-002 sets out the approval limits and escalation hierarchy for purchasing commitments at Northbridge Cycles [^r1][^r2]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]], all approval thresholds in this matrix are evaluated against the gross order value inclusive of VAT rather than the net basic cost [^r1]. Users are strictly prohibited from approving purchase orders they raised themselves, requiring escalation to higher authority whenever an order exceeds their delegation limit or requires independent sign-off [^r2].

## Clauses

### 1. Valuation Basis
Approval limits established in POL-APR-002 are evaluated on the gross order value, including applicable VAT, rather than net basic cost [^r1].

### 2. Self-Approval and Escalation
Users cannot self-approve orders they have raised regardless of their individual approval limit [^r2]. Any order exceeding a user's delegated authority must escalate to the next approver whose limit covers the total gross value [^r2].

POL-PUR-001 sets mandatory purchasing rules for all operations at the Manchester and Leeds sites using Ledgerline ERP [^r3]. Effective from 2026-04-01 under version 4.1, it governs purchase requisitions, approval limits, cost centre validation, and supplier qualifications [^r1]. It strictly mandates verified UN 38.3 certificates for lithium-cell components and enforces a 2% price variance cap against active rate contracts [^r2][^r16][^r20].

| Attribute | Details |
|---|---|
| Document Code | POL-PUR-001 [^r1] |
| Version | 4.1 [^r1] |
| Effective Date | 2026-04-01 [^r1] |
| Author | D. Okafor [^r1] |
| Approver | [[user-hweber|Henrik Weber]] [^r1] |
| Scope | Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01), Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) [^r3] |
| Status | Current [^r1] |

## Clauses

### 2. Scope
The purchase policy applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) through Ledgerline ERP [^r3].

### 3. Requests before orders
Every purchase must start with a purchase request in Ledgerline, unless it qualifies as a direct order under section 3.3 [^r4]. A purchase request specifies the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre bearing the expenditure [^r5]. A direct purchase order without a prior request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [^r6]. A purchase order created against a purchase request is not permitted to exceed the requested quantity [^r7].

### 4. Cost centres and budgets
Every purchase request and order must be charged to an open cost centre [^r8]. Ledgerline automatically saves any order booked against a closed cost centre as a Draft, and Draft orders are never sent to suppliers [^r9]. Staff must check cost centre status in Ledgerline using screen [[screen-fin-cc-01|FIN-CC-01]] or verify with Finance before raising an order [^r10].

### 5. Approval limits
Approval limits are evaluated against the gross value including VAT rather than the basic net value [^r11]. If an order exceeds the raiser's personal limit in the approval matrix ([[pol-apr-002|POL-APR-002]]), it must be approved by the next person up the line whose authority covers it [^r12]. Self-approval of purchase orders is strictly prohibited under all circumstances [^r13]. Approval of a purchase request covers the resulting purchase order provided the approver's personal limit covers the order's gross value [^r14].

### 6. Supplier qualification
Purchase orders may only be placed with suppliers that are active in the supplier master [^r15]. Lithium-cell parts (including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item with cell_safety = 1) may only be purchased from suppliers holding a verified, unexpired [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] in Ledgerline [^r2][^r16]. Before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [^r17]. Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts, and a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [^r18].

### 7. Prices
Orders must apply rates from current rate contracts, treating historical order prices as reference only [^r19]. Any purchase order placed at a price more than 2% above the rate contract requires written justification from the manager in the order remarks [^r2][^r20].

### 8. Tax
UK suppliers are charged UK VAT using [[data-tax-codes|tax codes]] ending in -UK, whereas non-UK suppliers are charged VAT via reverse charge using tax codes ending in -RC [^r21].

### 9. Records
An order must carry an official Ledgerline document number and attain Released status before the supplier is instructed to deliver or the requester is told the order is placed [^r22].

## Versions and conflicts
- Price tolerance over rate contract: Under version 4.1 (effective 2026-04-01), the allowed price tolerance is 2% with written justification in order remarks [^r2][^r20]. Previously, the tolerance threshold was 5% [^r2]. Kind: superseded.

UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] and [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must hold a verified certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and extends at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r1][^r3]. Expired certificates or those issued under superseded validity rules count as no certificate, preventing new order placement [^r2][^r4].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].

* **Older rule:** Under the prior rule, certificates were accepted under a 24-month validity period [^r4]. These certificates count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

runs.answer:
No, you cannot place the order [1][3]. 

Effective 1 September 2026 under AMD-SUP-2026-02 (which replaced POL-SUP-003 §4.4), Northbridge Cycles accepts a UN 38.3 certificate only if it was issued within the last 12 months and remains valid for at least 60 days after the order placement date [1][2][3]. 

Under the older, superseded rule, certificates issued within 24 months were accepted [1][3]. However, for any new orders placed from 1 September 2026, certificates meeting only the old 24-month rule count as no certificate in Ledgerline, which blocks new order placement [1][3]. Because the certificate was issued 18 months ago, it does not meet the current 12-month requirement [1][3].

AMD-SUP-2026-02 is an amendment to [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] effective 1 September 2026 that tightens the acceptance criteria for [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]][^r1][^r2]. Under this amendment, certificates must have been issued within the last 12 months and remain valid for at least 60 days following order placement[^r2]. It governs all new purchase orders placed for lithium-cell parts as of today, 26 October 2026[^r2][^r3].

## Clauses

### 1. What changes
Effective 1 September 2026, [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] §4.4 is replaced such that a [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2]. A certificate meeting the old rule of being issued within 24 months and not expired counts as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, whereas orders released before that date are not affected[^r3].

### 2. Why
The policy change was prompted by a July 2026 incident where a battery pack lot from a supplier with a 22-month-old test report failed Northbridge's incoming abuse test because the cell maker had changed[^r4].

Purchase staff must check the issue date and valid-to date of a lithium-cell part's certificate against the new rule before raising an order[^r5]. The [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] must run the certificate-expiry report per MAN-PUR-72 §22.6 on the first working day of each month with a 90-day window and notify every supplier whose UN 38.3 certificate expires within it[^r6]. UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] and [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must hold a verified certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and extends at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r1][^r3]. Expired certificates or those issued under superseded validity rules count as no certificate, preventing new order placement [^r2][^r4].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Today's rule (superseded):** From 1 September 2026 under AMD-SUP-2026-02, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3].
* **Older rule:** Under the prior rule, certificates were accepted under a 24-month validity period [^r4]. These certificates count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

POL-SUP-003 sets out Northbridge Cycles' mandatory standards and qualification rules for all suppliers. As of 1 September 2026, the policy incorporates updated compliance requirements for lithium battery documentation under [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]]. In force today, battery purchases governed by this policy require valid [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]] meeting strict issue-date and forward-validity criteria.

On 1 September 2026, Clause 4.4 of POL-SUP-003 was replaced by [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]] to require [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]] to have been issued within 12 months and valid for at least 60 days after order placement[^r1].

# AMD-SUP-2026-02 Amendment 2 to the Supplier Policy [[amd-sup-2026-02]]
| | |
|---|---|
| Document Code | AMD-SUP-2026-02 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Author | L. Moreno |
| Owner | Purchase department |
| Effective Date | 2026-09-01 |
| Status | CURRENT |

AMD-SUP-2026-02 is an amendment to [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] effective 1 September 2026 that tightens the acceptance criteria for [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificates]][^r1][^r2]. Under this amendment, certificates must have been issued within the last 12 months and remain valid for at least 60 days following order placement[^r2]. It governs all new purchase orders placed for lithium-cell parts as of today, 26 October 2026[^r2][^r3].

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document Code | AMD-SUP-2026-02 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Author | L. Moreno |
| Owner | Purchase department |
| Effective Date | 2026-09-01 |
| Status | CURRENT |

## Clauses

### 1. What changes
Effective 1 September 2026, [[pol-sup-003|POL-SUP-003]] §4.4 is replaced such that a [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months, and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2]. A certificate meeting the old rule of being issued within 24 months and not expired counts as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, whereas orders released before that date are not affected[^r3].

### 2. Why
The policy change was prompted by a July 2026 incident where a battery pack lot from a supplier with a 22-month-old test report failed Northbridge's incoming abuse test because the cell maker had changed[^r4].

### 3. What purchase staff must do
Purchase staff must check the issue date and valid-to date of a lithium-cell part's certificate against the new rule before raising an order[^r5]. The [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] must run the certificate-expiry report per MAN-PUR-72 §22.6 on the first working day of each month with a 90-day window and notify every supplier whose UN 38.3 certificate expires within it[^r6]. All other parts of POL-SUP-003 §4 remain in effect[^r7].

## Versions and conflicts
- **Today's rule (effective 2026-09-01)**: For new orders placed from 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and valid for at least 60 days after the order placement date[^r2][^r3].
- **Older rule (superseded)**: Certificates issued within 24 months and not expired were accepted under POL-SUP-003 §4.4; these now count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date are not affected[^r3].
- **Kind**: `superseded`[^r2][^r3].

# topic-un-38-3-certificates [[topic-un-38-3-certificates]]
| | |
|---|---|
| Topic | UN 38.3 Certificates |
| Applies to | Suppliers of lithium-cell parts |
| Policy reference | POL-PUR-001 §6, AMD-SUP-2026-02 §1 |
| System enforcement | Ledgerline order blocking |
| Monitoring role | Senior Buyer |
| Status | Current |

UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] and [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must hold a verified certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and extends at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r1][^r3]. Expired certificates or those issued under superseded validity rules count as no certificate, preventing new order placement [^r2][^r4].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Today's rule (superseded):** From 1 September 2026 under AMD-SUP-2026-02, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3].
* **Older rule:** Under the prior rule, certificates were accepted under a 24-month validity period [^r4]. These certificates count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

POL-PUR-001 sets mandatory purchasing rules for all operations at the Manchester and Leeds sites using Ledgerline ERP [^r3]. Effective from 2026-04-01 under version 4.1, it governs purchase requisitions, approval limits, cost centre validation, and supplier qualifications [^r1]. It strictly mandates verified UN 38.3 certificates for lithium-cell components and enforces a 2% price variance cap against active rate contracts [^r2][^r16][^r20].

| Version | 4.1 [^r1] |

| Scope | Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01), Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) [^r3] |
| Status | Current [^r1] |

## Clauses

### 2. Scope
The purchase policy applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) through Ledgerline ERP [^r3].

### 3. Requests before orders
Every purchase must start with a purchase request in Ledgerline, unless it qualifies as a direct order under section 3.3 [^r4]. A purchase request specifies the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre bearing the expenditure [^r5]. A direct purchase order without a prior request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [^r6]. A purchase order created against a purchase request is not permitted to exceed the requested quantity [^r7].

### 4. Cost centres and budgets
Every purchase request and order must be charged to an open cost centre [^r8]. Ledgerline automatically saves any order booked against a closed cost centre as a Draft, and Draft orders are never sent to suppliers [^r9]. Staff must check cost centre status in Ledgerline using screen [[screen-fin-cc-01|FIN-CC-01]] or verify with Finance before raising an order [^r10].

### 5. Approval limits
Approval limits are evaluated against the gross value including VAT rather than the basic net value [^r11]. If an order exceeds the raiser's personal limit in the approval matrix ([[pol-apr-002|POL-APR-002]]), it must be approved by the next person up the line whose authority covers it [^r12]. Self-approval of purchase orders is strictly prohibited under all circumstances [^r13]. Approval of a purchase request covers the resulting purchase order provided the approver's personal limit covers the order's gross value [^r14].

### 6. Supplier qualification
Purchase orders may only be placed with suppliers that are active in the supplier master [^r15]. Lithium-cell parts (including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item with cell_safety = 1) may only be purchased from suppliers holding a verified, unexpired [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] in Ledgerline [^r2][^r16]. Before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [^r17]. Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts, and a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [^r18].

### 7. Prices
Orders must apply rates from current rate contracts, treating historical order prices as reference only [^r19]. Any purchase order placed at a price more than 2% above the rate contract requires written justification from the manager in the order remarks [^r2][^r20].

### 8. Tax
UK suppliers are charged UK VAT using [[data-tax-codes|tax codes]] ending in -UK, whereas non-UK suppliers are charged VAT via reverse charge using tax codes ending in -RC [^r21].

### 9. Records
An order must carry an official Ledgerline document number and attain Released status before the supplier is instructed to deliver or the requester is told the order is placed [^r22].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].

Users cannot self-approve orders they have raised regardless of their individual approval limit [^r2]. Any order exceeding a user's delegated authority must escalate to the next approver whose limit covers the total gross value [^r2].

Effective from 2026-04-01 under version 4.1, it governs purchase requisitions, approval limits, cost centre validation, and supplier qualifications [^r1]. ## Clauses

### 2. Scope
The purchase policy applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) through Ledgerline ERP [^r3].

### 3. Requests before orders
Every purchase must start with a purchase request in Ledgerline, unless it qualifies as a direct order under section 3.3 [^r4]. A purchase request specifies the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre bearing the expenditure [^r5]. A direct purchase order without a prior request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [^r6]. A purchase order created against a purchase request is not permitted to exceed the requested quantity [^r7].

### 4. Cost centres and budgets
Every purchase request and order must be charged to an open cost centre [^r8]. Ledgerline automatically saves any order booked against a closed cost centre as a Draft, and Draft orders are never sent to suppliers [^r9]. Staff must check cost centre status in Ledgerline using screen [[screen-fin-cc-01|FIN-CC-01]] or verify with Finance before raising an order [^r10].

### 5. Approval limits
Approval limits are evaluated against the gross value including VAT rather than the basic net value [^r11]. If an order exceeds the raiser's personal limit in the approval matrix ([[pol-apr-002|POL-APR-002]]), it must be approved by the next person up the line whose authority covers it [^r12]. Self-approval of purchase orders is strictly prohibited under all circumstances [^r13]. Approval of a purchase request covers the resulting purchase order provided the approver's personal limit covers the order's gross value [^r14].

### 6. Supplier qualification
Purchase orders may only be placed with suppliers that are active in the supplier master [^r15]. Lithium-cell parts (including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item with cell_safety = 1) may only be purchased from suppliers holding a verified, unexpired [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] in Ledgerline [^r2][^r16]. Before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [^r17]. Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts, and a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [^r18].

### 7. Prices
Orders must apply rates from current rate contracts, treating historical order prices as reference only [^r19]. Any purchase order placed at a price more than 2% above the rate contract requires written justification from the manager in the order remarks [^r2][^r20].

### 8. Tax
UK suppliers are charged UK VAT using [[data-tax-codes|tax codes]] ending in -UK, whereas non-UK suppliers are charged VAT via reverse charge using tax codes ending in -RC [^r21].

### 9. Records
An order must carry an official Ledgerline document number and attain Released status before the supplier is instructed to deliver or the requester is told the order is placed [^r22].

POL-PUR-001 sets mandatory purchasing rules for all operations at the Manchester and Leeds sites using Ledgerline ERP [^r3]. Effective from 2026-04-01 under version 4.1, it governs purchase requisitions, approval limits, cost centre validation, and supplier qualifications [^r1]. It strictly mandates verified UN 38.3 certificates for lithium-cell components and enforces a 2% price variance cap against active rate contracts [^r2][^r16][^r20].

| Approver | [[user-hweber|Henrik Weber]] [^r1] |

| Status | Current [^r1] |

## Clauses

### 2. Scope
The purchase policy applies to every purchase made for the Manchester plant (NBC-MAN-01) and the Leeds unit (NBC-LDS-01) through Ledgerline ERP [^r3].

### 3. Requests before orders
Every purchase must start with a purchase request in Ledgerline, unless it qualifies as a direct order under section 3.3 [^r4]. A purchase request specifies the item, quantity, need-by date, warehouse, and the cost centre bearing the expenditure [^r5]. A direct purchase order without a prior request is permitted only when its gross value, including VAT, is £50,000 or less [^r6]. A purchase order created against a purchase request is not permitted to exceed the requested quantity [^r7].

### 4. Cost centres and budgets
Every purchase request and order must be charged to an open cost centre [^r8]. Ledgerline automatically saves any order booked against a closed cost centre as a Draft, and Draft orders are never sent to suppliers [^r9]. Staff must check cost centre status in Ledgerline using screen [[screen-fin-cc-01|FIN-CC-01]] or verify with Finance before raising an order [^r10].

### 5. Approval limits
Approval limits are evaluated against the gross value including VAT rather than the basic net value [^r11]. If an order exceeds the raiser's personal limit in the approval matrix ([[pol-apr-002|POL-APR-002]]), it must be approved by the next person up the line whose authority covers it [^r12]. Self-approval of purchase orders is strictly prohibited under all circumstances [^r13]. Approval of a purchase request covers the resulting purchase order provided the approver's personal limit covers the order's gross value [^r14].

### 6. Supplier qualification
Purchase orders may only be placed with suppliers that are active in the supplier master [^r15]. Lithium-cell parts (including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any item with cell_safety = 1) may only be purchased from suppliers holding a verified, unexpired [[topic-un-38-3-certificates|UN 38.3 certificate]] in Ledgerline [^r2][^r16]. Before placing orders with a new supplier, the supplier must be formally onboarded under POL-SUP-003 [^r17]. Purchasers must prefer suppliers with current rate contracts, and a cheaper quotation from a new supplier does not justify switching suppliers for a lithium-cell part [^r18].

### 7. Prices
Orders must apply rates from current rate contracts, treating historical order prices as reference only [^r19]. Any purchase order placed at a price more than 2% above the rate contract requires written justification from the manager in the order remarks [^r2][^r20].

### 8. Tax
UK suppliers are charged UK VAT using [[data-tax-codes|tax codes]] ending in -UK, whereas non-UK suppliers are charged VAT via reverse charge using tax codes ending in -RC [^r21].

### 9. Records
An order must carry an official Ledgerline document number and attain Released status before the supplier is instructed to deliver or the requester is told the order is placed [^r22].

## Versions and conflicts
- Price tolerance over rate contract: Under version 4.1 (effective 2026-04-01), the allowed price tolerance is 2% with written justification in order remarks [^r2][^r20]. Previously, the tolerance threshold was 5% [^r2]. Kind: superseded.

UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] and [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must hold a verified certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and extends at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r1][^r3]. Expired certificates or those issued under superseded validity rules count as no certificate, preventing new order placement [^r2][^r4].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].

## Versions and conflicts

* **Today's rule (superseded):** From 1 September 2026 under AMD-SUP-2026-02, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3].
* **Older rule:** Under the prior rule, certificates were accepted under a 24-month validity period [^r4]. These certificates count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, though orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

UN 38.3 certificates verify lithium-cell transport safety compliance for parts procured by Northbridge Cycles [^r1]. Under [[pol-pur-001|POL-PUR-001]] and [[amd-sup-2026-02|AMD-SUP-2026-02]], suppliers providing lithium-cell items must hold a verified certificate in Ledgerline that was issued within the last 12 months and extends at least 60 days beyond the purchase order date [^r1][^r3]. Expired certificates or those issued under superseded validity rules count as no certificate, preventing new order placement [^r2][^r4].

## Requirements and Ledgerline verification

Suppliers of lithium-cell parts, including battery packs, hub motors, chargers, and any items with `cell_safety = 1`, must hold a valid UN 38.3 certificate uploaded and verified in Ledgerline before orders can be placed [^r1]. Under POL-PUR-001 §6.2, an expired UN 38.3 certificate counts as no certificate in Ledgerline [^r2].

Under AMD-SUP-2026-02, effective 1 September 2026, a UN 38.3 certificate is accepted only if issued within the last 12 months and its valid-to date is at least 60 days after the date the purchase order is placed [^r3]. Certificates issued under the prior 24-month validity rule count as no certificate for new orders placed from 1 September 2026, although orders released prior to that date remain valid [^r4].

## Purchasing staff responsibilities

On the first working day of each month, the [[role-pur-senior-buyer|senior buyer]] runs the certificate-expiry report (MAN-PUR-72 §22.6) with a 90-day window to contact suppliers with expiring UN 38.3 certificates [^r5].
